modern: Whether the universe is a concourse of atoms, or nature is a system, let this first be established: that I am a part of the whole which is governed by nature; next, that I am in a way closely related to the parts which are of the same kind as myself. For if I remember this, since I am a part, I shall be discontented with none of the things which are assigned to me out of the whole; for nothing is harmful to the part if it is for the advantage of the whole. For the whole contains nothing which is not for its advantage; and all natures indeed have this common principle, but the nature of the universe has this principle besides, that it cannot be compelled even by any external cause to generate anything harmful to itself. By remembering, then, that I am a part of such a whole, I shall be content with everything that happens. And since I am in a way closely related to the parts which are of the same kind as myself, I shall do nothing unsociable, but I shall rather direct myself to the things which are of the same kind as myself, and I shall turn all my efforts to the common good, and turn them away from the opposite. Now, if these things are done so, life must flow on happily, just as you may observe that the life of a citizen is happy who continues a course of action which is to the advantage of his fellow citizens, and is content with whatever the state may assign to him.
original: Whether the universe is [a concourse of] atoms, or nature [is a system], let this first be established, that I am a part of the whole which is governed by nature; next, I am in a manner intimately related to the parts which are of the same kind with myself. For remembering this, inasmuch as I am a part, I shall be discontented with none of the things which are assigned to me out of the whole; for nothing is injurious to the part if it is for the advantage of the whole. For the whole contains nothing which is not for its advantage; and all natures indeed have this common principle, but the nature of the universe has this principle besides, that it cannot be compelled even by any external cause to generate anything harmful to itself. By remembering, then, that I am a part of such a whole, I shall be content with everything that happens. And inasmuch as I am in a manner intimately related to the parts which are of the same kind with myself, I shall do nothing unsocial, but I shall rather direct myself to the things which are of the same kind with myself, and I shall turn all my efforts to the common interest, and divert them from the contrary. Now, if these things are done so, life must flow on happily, just as thou mayst observe that the life of a citizen is happy, who continues a course of action which is advantageous to his fellow-citizens, and is content with whatever the state may assign to him.

explained.summary:
Whether the universe is ordered by a purpose or is just chance, Marcus starts from two facts. You are a part of a larger whole, and you are related to other people, who share the same nature and the same reason.

The first means you can accept what comes your way, since nothing that serves the whole truly harms a part of it. The second means you should never act against others, but put your effort into the common good. Live like that and life runs smoothly, just as a good citizen thrives by serving their city and accepting whatever role it gives them.
explained.today: A nurse handed an unwanted night shift, or the volunteer given the dull job at the school fair, can treat it as their share of something larger instead of a personal injustice, and still put their effort into doing it well for everyone else.
